title: Make it possible to turn off automatic txout ordering

traits.after: BIP-69 by default; opt-out keeps recipient-entered output order
traits.evidence: simple_config.py: WALLET_SORT_TX_OUTPUTS = ConfigVar('sort_tx_outputs', default=True, ...); wallet.py: PartialTransaction.from_io(list(coins), list(outputs), BIP69_sort = self.config.WALLET_SORT_TX_OUTPUTS)

traits.after: BIP-69 by default; opt-out leaves inputs in wallet coin order
traits.evidence: same from_io(..., BIP69_sort=...) call: BIP69_sort toggles sorting of both inputs and outputs

summary: Adds a Qt tx-editor toggle that turns off BIP-69 sorting, so a user-built send-max transaction keeps its outputs (and inputs) in the order given instead of lexicographic order.
notes: Opt-in; default stays BIP-69. As written, the patch only touches the 'spend max' branch of make_unsigned_transaction (coinchooser-built txs with change stay BIP-69 sorted). Stale since 2024: it targets old code and would need rebasing. The config text has a TODO to switch to randomized ordering later.

title: Taproot swaps

traits.after: P2TR (two-leaf tapscript: claim/refund) when the swap server advertises taproot-v1; P2WSH fallback
traits.evidence: submarine_swaps.py: lockup_address = ... if protocol == TAPROOT_SWAP_PROTOCOL else script_to_p2wsh(redeem_script); use_taproot = TAPROOT_SWAP_PROTOCOL in transport.protocols

traits.after: P2TR script-path (claim/refund) or P2TR key-path MuSig2 (cooperative)
traits.evidence: add_txin_info: txin.tap_script_signing_data = TapScriptSigningData(script=..., control_block=...); sig_dummy = bytes(64)
transaction.py: sighash = txin.sighash if txin.sighash is not None else Sighash.DEFAULT; cooperative: tx.serialize_preimage(0, sighash=Sighash.DEFAULT)
cooperative claim: PartialTransaction.from_io([txin], [txout], locktime=0, version=2, BIP69_sort=False); validator requires network_tx.locktime == 0

traits.before: built by txbatcher (may be batched with other sweeps/payments, wallet change output)
traits.after: cooperative claim/refund: standalone 1-input 1-output tx, nSequence 0xFFFFFFFD (script-path fallback still goes through txbatcher)
traits.evidence: validator: len(inputs) != 1 or len(outputs) != 1 -> 'cooperative transaction shape is not canonical'; tests assert txbatcher.add_sweep_input.assert_not_called() for cooperative path

summary: Swap lockup outputs become P2TR instead of P2WSH, and swap claims/refunds become taproot spends (64-byte SIGHASH_DEFAULT sigs); cooperative MuSig2 claims are single-input single-output txs with nLockTime 0.
notes: Swap path only (submarine swaps, client and swapserver plugin). Draft PR. Taproot is used automatically when the server offers 'taproot-v1', and the cooperative key-path spend when it offers 'taproot-cooperative-v1'. The nlocktime 'before' refers to reverse-swap claims built by txbatcher with locktime=None; forward-swap refunds keep using the swap CLTV height. Needs an unreleased electrum-ecc with MuSig2. I read only the claim/refund construction and negotiation parts of this ~4900-line diff.

title: submarine_swaps: Reintroduce support for the old submarine swap protocol

traits.before: one unified witness script for all swaps (reverse-swap template)
traits.after: adds the v1 forward-swap witness script (HASH160 preimage / CLTV refund template) for swaps made with v1 clients
traits.evidence: submarine_swaps.py: _construct_swap_scriptcode_v1(... values={1: ripemd(payment_hash), 4: server_pubkey, 6: locktime, 9: client_pubkey}); 'capabilities': [ CAP_FORWARD_V1 ]

summary: When Electrum runs as a swap server, it accepts old-flow (v1) forward swaps, so its claim transactions spend P2WSH outputs with a different HTLC witness script.
notes: Swapserver plugin path only (opt-in). The external v1 client funds the lockup output; Electrum's claim tx reveals the v1 script in its witness. Input type stays P2WSH; only the script template differs.

title: commands: accept script(...) outputs in payto/paytomany, like the GUI

traits.before: yes (GUI payee field only, via script(...))
traits.evidence: commands.py + payment_identifier.py: shared parse_script(); e.g. `electrum payto "script(OP_RETURN 48656c6c6f)" 0`

summary: CLI/RPC payto and paytomany can now create transactions with arbitrary script outputs such as OP_RETURN, which before was possible only from the GUI.
notes: Opt-in (user must specify the script output). Default transactions do not change; the effect is that OP_RETURN outputs become easy for RPC/scripted users and merchants.

title: WIP: payjoin as sender

traits.after: BIP78 sender: when paying a pj= URI, broadcasts the receiver's proposal with extra receiver input(s) and adjusted change
traits.evidence: transaction.py: class PayjoinTransaction ... query_string += '&additionalfeeoutputindex=' ...; validate_payjoin_proposal() checks version/locktime/nsequence unchanged

traits.after: receiver-chosen order for payjoin txs (the proposal is not re-sorted)
traits.evidence: validate_payjoin_proposal: '#TODO: check if the order of inputs is important'; no BIP69_sort applied to the proposal

summary: Paying a BIP78 payjoin invoice would put a two-party transaction on chain containing the receiver's input(s), in the receiver's input order, instead of an Electrum-only BIP-69 transaction.
notes: Draft since 2020; it targets the old Kivy/Qt code and is effectively dormant, so it is unlikely to merge as-is. It applies only when the URI has pj=. The validator requires one uniform nSequence and one uniform input script type, so single_type is preserved. nVersion, nLockTime and the sender's nSequence must stay unchanged.
